claims.summary: first_word_after (L89) uses split_whitespace + a manual alphanumeric filter (L92); if a marker is followed by a punctuation-heavy string or a non-standard whitespace char (like a non-breaking space) before the next word, find might skip the verb or return empty, so followed_by_explicit_exact_token_relation (L64) fails and the marker is stripped.
claims.disposition: Hypothesis (non-breaking space/punctuation makes first_word_after L89 skip the verb, stripping the marker) REFUTED by source (not domesticated). split_whitespace L91 treats U+00A0 as whitespace; trim_matches L92 strips a leading U+FEFF; find skips punctuation-only chunks. Punctuation case grounded by existing test L2899; her non-breaking-space case by a NEW regression (U+00A0 + U+FEFF -> `denotes` found, marker preserved). Strips only when no alphanumeric word follows (fail-closed).
